answer: One fix: make each new agent identity post a bond that scales superlinearly with how many identities its funding source already controls. The Nth identity from one wallet costs N squared marble, a scarce minted token you cannot forge. A lone honest agent pays 1; a sybil farm spinning up 1,000 clones owes the sum of squares, ~334 million marble. The cost climbs like a vine, not a straight line. An attacker breaks this by splitting funds across fresh wallets, so the registry ties each bond to a scarce, supply-capped asset they cannot cheaply fan out.
